questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I think it was a mix of different things. I really wanted to travel and experience studying in another country.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an english speaking country with options to study astrophysics but also explore the country. I chose New Zealand because of its beautiful nature, opportunities to study, and because I have a family connection in the country as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely the best six months! I have no regrets choosing New Zealand and wish I could go back to experience it all again.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the information I needed was at the university website. Sometimes i needed to search a bit but it wasn't too bad. The visa was a bit confusing to me though, because I wanted to go a couple months before studying, which unfortunately was not possible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up at the airport which was included in my accommodation at the uni halls. At uni we had an internation introduction where we got most of the information we needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: As an international student you are guaranteed a place in one of the uni halls. I had my own room and shared kitchen, shower and bathroom with four other international students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no options for meal plans in the hall I was in, but I think some of the other halls have them. We had a kitchen the most basic things. No oven unfortunately.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Even if it is a bit expensive I would definitely say that it is worth it. The accommodation itself might not be the most amazing, but I met most of my friends here. There are a lot of small events for the halls, where it is easy to meet a lot of new people in the beginning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of the process was easy enough but it was a but I had some trouble uploading my evidence for english language proficiency because I didn't take a language test. I also had a bit of trouble changing the courses I chose, when some were not available.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to login to an online portal and fill out a form.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an email you could write which I did, but they did not help that much.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I wanted were not available, but besides that I got all the courses I signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't do it the day before :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the physics courses at home are definitely better but some of the other courses I had were great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two first year courses(100 level) which were of course not too hard. The physics courses (300 level) was probably the same level as at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are less tutorials here and the lectures are a bit different. The lecturers use power points a lot more instead of writing on the chalk board. I also think we had more assignments than I am used to for some courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Theoretical and Observational Cosmology (ASTR332), Laser Physics and Modern Optics(PHYS323), Antarctica: The Cold Continent(ANTA102) and Witchcraft, Magic and the Dead(ANTH108)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Witchcraft, Magic and the Dead!! It was a lot of fun, very interesting, the teacher was great and I learned so much that I thought I wouldn't. A lot of reading and writing though but it is definitely worth it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy some stuff for my room

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The vegetables are pretty expensive. Public transport is really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a fitness centre with gym and classes. It is free to sign up and most of the classes are free as well. The university has a lot of clubs and social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The fitness centre was great. Lots of clubs have opportunities to go on trips as well. The tramping club lets you rent gear which is really nice and can save you a lot of money.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Get out and see the country - the South Island is absolutely beautiful! Milford Sound was one of the most amazing places I have ever been.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy I would say. The Kiwis are friendly - maybe the accent can be a bit of a challenge in the beginning I would say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The people at the university are not necessarily the most social and some of them have known each other for years which doesn't make it easier. By best advice would be to just try and talk to them anyways because they are usually really friendly. Also try and join some clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The kiwi accent. Also they cancel events really fast and move them around as they want to. A little rain might stop an event...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Kiwis are really friendly. The Maori culture and language is pretty cool as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it - time is passing so fast! And don't be afraid to travel to the other side of the world. The flight might be horrible but it is worth it. Chose as many "fun" courses as possible instead of what you are usually studying.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save a lot of money for travelling. New Zealand is not cheap and you might want a lot of outdoor gear all of the sudden.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world including the kiwis. Studying different courses from home, and seeing the insanely beautiful nature of New Zealand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The two day trip I went on with the Tramping Club. I still don't know how I survived.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to New Zealand - you won't regret it!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
